title: Taking the horse and wagon, and leading horses at the auction
summary: He hitched a neighbor's horses and ran off with the wagon, and earned quarters leading horses at the Saturday auction.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: back of the place that we lived at, where he kept his horses at, so I used to go down there and when he hitch 'em up, get a wagon. I would help him. So I learned how to hitch up the horses and the wagon by myself, so one day I decided that I was gonna take the wagon out myself. So I hitched up the horses, hitched them to the wagon, and off I took. Got all the kids, put 'em in the wagon...we ridin' around havin' a ball. And the man was goin' crazy lookin' for his horses and the wagon. He didn't know what happened to them. We rode around for two...three hours. Everybody was lookin' for the man's wagon. So finally we came back with it. He was so glad to see us. My momma like to beat the devil out of me for runnin' off with the man's wagon and horses 'cause she wasn't scared I'd get hurt.

So I...uh...used to be a place up the street a few blocks where they sold horses at--a regular auction place. So I used to go up there and hang around on the weekends...on Saturday when they have the auction. So you get a quarter if you lead the horse out, you know. So I was so little and skinny...heaven look at me now. Don't nobody believe that I weighed about ninety pounds. So I would ask the people up there, "Let me make a quarter. Let me lead your horse."
Say, "Get away, kid. You get killed. This horse is a bad horse. You can't lead him."
"Oh, yes I can. Just gimme...just gimme the quarter. I'll bring him around. I'll lead him around."
So some of the fellows said, "Okay. Okay, kid. All right."
